import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.25

by V. M. Kopytov

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.25»

/--
The quotient of any nontrivial solvable linearly ordered group $G$ by its derived subgroup
$[G,G]$ is non-periodic. Here the linear order is invariant under multiplication on both sides,
and non-periodic means that the abelianization $G/[G,G]$ is not a torsion group.

The nontriviality assumption excludes the trivial group, whose abelianization is periodic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.25» :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G]
      [IsSolvable G] [Nontrivial G], ¬ Monoid.IsTorsion (Abelianization G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.25»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted a linearly ordered group as a group with a `LinearOrder` whose left and right multiplication maps are monotone, encoded by `MulLeftMono` and `MulRightMono`; for group translations this gives invariance in both directions.
Used Mathlib's `Abelianization G`, which is defined as the quotient of `G` by its commutator (derived) subgroup.
Rendered non-periodic as `¬ Monoid.IsTorsion (Abelianization G)`, matching the stipulated meaning that the quotient has an element of infinite order.
Explicitly required `Nontrivial G` to exclude the trivial group, whose abelianization is torsion.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.25

by V. M. Kopytov

Prove that the factor-group of any soluble linearly ordered group by its derived
subgroup is non-periodic.

Here a linearly ordered group is a group with a linear (total) order that is
invariant under multiplication on both sides. A group is periodic if every
element has finite order.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.25»

/--
Prove that the factor-group of any soluble linearly ordered group by its derived
subgroup is non-periodic.

That is, if $G$ is a nontrivial soluble group with a linear order invariant under
left and right multiplication, then $G / [G, G]$ has an element of infinite order.
The trivial group is excluded since its (trivial) abelianization is periodic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.25» (G : Type*) [Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G]
    [IsSolvable G] [Nontrivial G] :
    ¬ Monoid.IsTorsion (G ⧸ commutator G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.25»

modeling_decisions: 'Linearly ordered group' is read in Kopytov's (Russian-school) sense as a bi-ordered group: `LinearOrder G` together with `MulLeftMono G` (left invariance: a ≤ b → c*a ≤ c*b) and `MulRightMono G` (right invariance: a ≤ b → a*c ≤ b*c). Mathlib's bundled `IsOrderedMonoid` could not be used since it requires `CommMonoid`.
'Factor-group by its derived subgroup' is stated literally as `G ⧸ commutator G` (where `commutator G = ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆`); this is definitionally `Abelianization G`.
'Non-periodic' is `¬ Monoid.IsTorsion (G ⧸ commutator G)`, i.e. not every element has finite order, equivalently some element has infinite order (`Monoid.not_isTorsion_iff`).
The trivial group is excluded via `[Nontrivial G]` as required by the decomposition table (its abelianization is trivial, hence periodic); this is explained in the theorem docstring.
Since the statement is an imperative 'Prove that …' rather than a yes/no question, the repository's plain `theorem … : P := by sorry` style is used instead of `answer(sorry) ↔ …`.

`LinearOrder` bundles decidability data, but since G and its instances are universally quantified hypotheses of the theorem, any bi-invariant total order can classically be packaged this way, so no generality is lost.

by its derived subgroup $G' = [G, G]$ is non-periodic, i.e. it contains an
element of infinite order.

trivial, hence periodic.

    ¬ Monoid.IsTorsion (G ⧸ commutator G) := by

this is the same as asking that $G$ be infinite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.25» :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G],
      Nontrivial G → IsSolvable G → ¬ Monoid.IsTorsion (Abelianization G) := by
  sorry
